findings.headline: THE LOAD-BEARING ENGINE CLAIM IS NOW PRIMARY: the stock Sionna RT path solver contains no physical-optics surface integral over induced currents.
findings.what_is_true: Machine counts over the complete text layer of the 59-page technical report v2: 'physical optics' 0, standalone 'PO' 0, 'induced current' 0, 'surface current' 0, 'Kirchhoff' 0, 'radar cross section' 0, 'RCS' 0, 'dBsm' 0, 'radar equation' 0. 'surface integral' returns exactly ONE hit and it is a bibliography entry, not a method: reference [26] 'Wikipedia. Surface integral. Accessed November-2025.', cited on p.35 for the radio-map area integral. The 5-page founding paper returns 0 for every one of the same terms.
findings.quote: p58 references: '[26] Wikipedia. Surface integral. Accessed November-2025. [Online]. Available: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surface_integral 35'

findings.headline: What the stock solver computes at a surface, part 1 - SPECULAR = Fresnel coefficient multiplication.
findings.what_is_true: Appendix A.7 'Specular Reflection and Refraction' derives r_perp, r_par, t_perp, t_par as the classical Fresnel ratios (eq. 127), gives their vacuum-incidence simplification (eq. 128), and applies them as a 2x2 diagonal matrix to the incident field (eq. 129-130). Snell's law is eq. (121). Appendix A.7.1 replaces (128) with single-layer slab coefficients (eq. 131-133) parameterised by slab thickness d. Term counts: 'Fresnel' 8, 'specular' 101, 'reflection coefficient' 1, 'Snell' 1.
findings.quote: p46: 'The Fresnel equations provide relationships between the incident, reflected, and refracted field components for sqrt(|eta1/eta2|) sin(theta1) < 1:' followed by eq. (127) r_perp = (sqrt(eta1) cos(theta1) - sqrt(eta2) cos(theta2)) / (sqrt(eta1) cos(theta1) + sqrt(eta2) cos(theta2)). p44: 'We assume in the following description that both materials are uniform non-magnetic dielectrics, i.e. mu_r = 1.'

findings.headline: What the stock solver computes at a surface, part 2 - DIFFUSE = an empirical scattering-coefficient model, not a current integral.
findings.what_is_true: Appendix A.9 models the diffusely scattered field with a scattering coefficient S in [0,1], a reflection reduction factor R = sqrt(1 - S^2) that multiplies the Fresnel coefficients, an XPD-controlled polarisation mixing matrix, and a normalised scattering pattern f_s (Lambertian eq.172, directive eq.173, backscattering eq.174). The scattered-field equation (168) is attributed to reference [42, Eq. 9], a Degli-Esposti-type empirical model. No induced current, no Stratton-Chu / Kirchhoff integral, no aperture integration anywhere.
findings.quote: p50: 'Since most surfaces give both specular and diffuse reflections, we denote by S^2 the fraction of the reflected energy that is diffusely scattered, where S in [0,1] is the so-called scattering coefficient [41]. ... Whenever a material has a scattering coefficient S > 0, the Fresnel reflection coefficients in (127) must be multiplied by (164).'  p51: 'f_s(k_i, k_s, n) is the scattering pattern, which has similarities with the BSDF in computer graphics'  p51: the normalisation condition (171) 'ensures the power balance between the incoming, reflected, and refracted fields.'

findings.headline: The stock solver supports exactly four interaction types, and says so.
findings.what_is_true: Section 2.3: specular reflection (R), diffuse reflection (S), refraction (T), diffraction (D); the set is written I = {R, S, T, D}. Diffraction is the UTD heuristic extension to finitely conducting wedges (A.8), first order only. 'UTD' 3 hits, 'diffract*' 143 hits.
findings.quote: p9: 'Sionna RT currently supports four types of interactions with scene objects: Specular reflection (R) ... Diffuse reflection (S) ... Refraction (T) ... Diffraction (D)'.  p29 (Sec 3.4 Current Limitations): 'The path solver supports only first-order diffraction and does not handle paths that contain both diffraction and diffuse reflection.' and 'calculating the electric field along these high-order diffraction paths remains an open problem, and as a result, high-order diffraction is not currently supported.'

findings.headline: SCOPE GUARD: the technical report DOES use the acronym SBR, 48 times - but as a candidate generator, never as SBR+PO.
findings.what_is_true: Sionna RT's SBR shoots rays on a Fibonacci lattice, samples ONE interaction type per hit, spawns exactly ONE outgoing ray, and hands specular-suffix candidates to an image method that repositions the vertices. It is a geometric path search, not a current-integration scheme. Anyone who reads 'Sionna has no SBR' in our documents reads a false statement; the true statement is 'Sionna's SBR carries no PO surface integral'.
findings.quote: p1 abstract: 'For CIRs, Sionna RT integrates shooting and bouncing of rays (SBR) with the image method and uses a hashing-based mechanism to efficiently eliminate duplicate paths. Radio maps are computed using a purely SBR-based approach.'  p11: 'Notably, at each interaction of a ray with a surface in the scene, only one scattered ray is spawned, as spawning multiple rays would result in an exponential increase in the number of rays, quickly overwhelming the available computational resources.'  p12: 'Intuitively, SBR pre-selects path candidates in the vicinity of the transmitter and receiver for the image method to compute corresponding valid paths to be returned by the solver.'
findings.note: Confirms the memory note 'sionna2 RT-RCS claim scope' from the primary source.

findings.headline: The technical report is a propagation document, not a sensing document - and its word 'target' means a receiver endpoint.
findings.what_is_true: 'sensing' 0 hits, 'ISAC' 0 hits, 'drone'/'UAV' 0 hits. 'target' 85 hits, all meaning a path endpoint.
findings.quote: p11: 'A path solver aims to determine a set of paths that connect two endpoints in a scene ... We consider a scene with a single source located at s in R^3 and N_T targets at t_k in R^3'
findings.note: Guard: never quote the report's 'target' as if it meant a radar target.

findings.headline: VERSION TRAP: the founding paper describes v0.14, an architecture we do not run, and contains no EM equations at all.
findings.what_is_true: 5-page overview of Sionna v0.14 (Mitsuba 3 for intersections, TensorFlow for field transforms, no refraction). Term counts: Fresnel 0, physical optics 0, RCS 0, SBR 0, UTD 0, dBsm 0, reflection coefficient 0, Snell 0. All EM detail is deferred to the website EM primer (footnote 3).
findings.quote: p3: 'Sionna RT supports specular and diffuse reflections (i.e., scattering) as well as first-order diffraction. A detailed explanation of the involved computing steps is provided on the Sionna documentation website.'  and 'For future releases, it is planned to add refraction as well as support for RIS while still ensuring differentiability of all involved processing steps.'
findings.action: Cite the founding paper only for provenance. For solver behaviour cite the technical report v2, which matches Sionna 2.0.1.

findings.what_we_said: prior_work/src/pw04_data.py L6 and L121, and the published notebook prior_work/pw04_rcs_solution_by_target.ipynb L74: '원문 검증 결과 Sionna·ray-tracing·mesh 를 전혀 쓰지 않음(표적을 추상 복소계수로 표현). Sionna 표에서 제외.'

Independent counts over the full 41-page text layer: Sionna 13, ray-trac* 7, mesh 2, Blender 1, XML 1. Four figures (6, 7, 9, 11) are Sionna RT outputs. The paper cites the Sionna RT Technical Report as [72].

findings.quote: p23: 'The ToI and UAVs are modeled as simplified 3-D mesh objects imported into Sionna. These meshes are obtained by simplifying publicly available 3-D models in Blender and exporting them in Sionna's XML format, which keeps the ray-tracing scene lightweight while enabling flexible material assignment.'

findings.headline: WHY the two readings disagreed: pw04 read the analytical model and stopped there.
findings.what_is_true: pw04's DESCRIPTION is true of Section II-C and false of the case studies. Section II-C models the scene as discrete scatterers whose complex coefficients absorb the RCS - literally pw04's 'abstract complex coefficient'. Sections V-VII then ALSO run a site-specific Sionna RT scene with imported UAV meshes. One paper, two target representations; pw04 generalised from the first to the whole paper.
findings.quote: p5: 'We model the scene as a collection of discrete scatterers, each with its own radar cross section (RCS), propagation delay, Doppler shift, and direction.'  p6 after eq. (11a-11b): 'the frequency-dependent complex coefficients {alpha_{m,n}, beta_{c,n}} capture the combined effects of RCS, path loss, and multipath-induced phase variations'
findings.note: The correct rewrite keeps BOTH halves: stochastic model = abstract coefficient; site-specific case study = Sionna RT with meshes.

One work, one error.

findings.verdict: VERIFIED (3 of 4 clauses) / clause 4 UNSUPPORTED AS WRITTEN
findings.headline: H1 stands except for the words 'stock Fresnel', which the paper never says.
findings.claim: H1: Clutter-Aware ISAC imports meshes into Sionna and accepts stock Fresnel, motivated by keeping the scene lightweight, with no scattering audit.
findings.what_is_true: CLAUSE 1 'imports meshes into Sionna' - VERIFIED verbatim (S11). CLAUSE 2 'motivated by keeping the scene lightweight' - VERIFIED verbatim; the paper's own words are 'which keeps the ray-tracing scene lightweight while enabling flexible material assignment'. CLAUSE 3 'no scattering audit' - VERIFIED and strong: 'validat*' 0 hits in 41 pages, 'dBsm' 0, 'permittivity' 0, 'conductivit*' 0, 'physical optics' 0, 'measurement campaign' 0, 'ground truth' 0. No RCS value is ever assigned to the UAV mesh; no comparison to measurement or to another EM solver. CLAUSE 4 'accepts STOCK FRESNEL' - NOT SUPPORTED AS WRITTEN: 'Fresnel' 0 hits; the paper never states which material or reflection model it assigns, only 'flexible material assignment'. That Sionna RT's stock reflection is Fresnel is OUR inference from the technical report (S04), not this paper's statement.
findings.quote: p23: 'The maximum interaction depth for Sionna is set to three, so each ray undergoes at most three interactions with scene objects. ... Sionna defines the LoS as a direct Tx-Rx path, so for monostatic sensing, the target echoes appear as reflected and scattered paths that interact with the target object, even when a geometric LoS exists.'
findings.numbers_evidence: p25 caption: 'Fig. 7. Spatial pseudo-spectra and RDMs before and after slow-time filterings in the Sionna RT-generated mixed-clutter case. ... SCNR = -63.5 dB.'  p23 caption: 'Fig. 5. Spatial pseudo-spectra and RDMs before and after slow-time filterings with both cold and hot clutters. ... SCNR = -47.4 dB.'  DO NOT SWAP: Fig. 5 is the stochastic scatterer model, Fig. 7 is the Sionna RT scene.
findings.action: Rewrite clause 4 as 'does not state or audit its surface model'.

findings.headline: Our report-facing prose says the CFAR vocabulary is absent; it is present 4 times. The census was right.
findings.what_we_said: docs/DRONE_ISAC_PRIOR_READING.md L514-515: 'clutter = SCNR 과 정성적 RDM 뿐, Pd/Pfa/ROC 0건, ECA/CLEAN/CAF 언급 0회'.
findings.what_is_true: Counted here from scratch over the full 41-page text, trusting neither of our files. cfar = 4, false-alarm = 3 - the census was right and the prose is wrong if read as 'CFAR absent'. ECA = 0, CLEAN = 0, CAF = 0 - the prose is right there. ROC = 0, 'detection probability' = 0, 'probability of detection' = 0, P_FA / P_D symbol forms = 0 - the prose is right there too. All 4 CFAR and all 3 false-alarm mentions are REVIEW PROSE about technique families (Sec. III baseline pipeline, Sec. IV amplitude statistics); none is applied to produce a number.
findings.quote: p10: 'To maintain a prescribed false-alarm probability, range-Doppler constant false-alarm rate (CFAR) detectors estimate the local interference power from neighboring training cells around the cell under test and adapt the threshold accordingly. Representative CFAR variants and comparative studies can be found in [49].'  p11: 'Clutter amplitude statistics depend on the underlying scattering mechanisms and are often characterized by their tail behavior, which directly impacts CFAR thresholding and false-alarm performance.'
findings.narrowest_supportable_form: 'Clutter-Aware ISAC discusses CFAR as a review topic (4 mentions) and names the false-alarm probability (3 mentions) but reports no Pd, no Pfa value and no ROC anywhere in its 41 pages; its quantitative sensing results are SCNR values plus qualitative RDM / beampattern / angle-Doppler maps. It never mentions ECA, CLEAN or CAF.'
findings.action: Replace L514-515 with narrowest_supportable_form. This is an E1-shaped negative claim and must not survive as written.

findings.headline: '39 pages, no ADC' - the PDF is 41 pages and ADC IS named.
findings.what_we_said: docs/DRONE_ISAC_PRIOR_READING.md L36, L425: '39쪽 튜토리얼' / '39쪽 전체에 ADC·양자화 모델이 없다'.
findings.what_is_true: 41 pages (measured). 'ADC' appears once, on p5, as a named receive-chain stage. 'quantiz*' appears once, on p33, about CSI quantization errors in beamforming ([91] Choi et al.), not an ADC model.
findings.quote: p5: 'After analog-to-digital conversion (ADC), CP removal, and a fast Fourier transform (FFT), the received signal y_n[l] in C^{N_r} at subcarrier n and OFDM symbol l is represented as ...'
findings.narrowest_supportable_form: 'The 41-page tutorial names the ADC as a receive-chain stage but contains no ADC quantization / bit-depth model.'

findings.headline: md-rt is NOT stock Sionna - its second stated contribution replaces spherical ray sampling with a cone.
findings.what_we_said: H6: 'md-rt (IEEE ICCT 2025): Sionna STOCK, propeller material Wood, claims only spectrogram ridge positions'.
findings.what_is_true: The EM side is stock; the SAMPLER is not. Contribution 2 in the paper's own list is an explicit modification of the ray launcher. Calling it 'stock Sionna' understates what they built and is exactly the sort of sentence a reviewer catches.
findings.version: PUBLISHED: 2025 IEEE 25th International Conference on Communication Technology (ICCT), DOI 10.1109/ICCT67417.2025.11374154 (PDF metadata Subject field + page-1 footer). 6 pages. NOT a preprint.
findings.quote: p1 contribution 2: 'We propose an improved directional ray-tracing strategy based on Sionna RT, which replaces spherical sampling with conical sampling to enhance path density and distribution accuracy in critical regions.'  p3: 'We utilize the built-in Fibonacci sampling function provided by the Sionna framework to generate N uniformly distributed sampling points on the unit square [0,1]^2 ... The sample points are first projected onto the surface of a cone defined in the local coordinate system'  and 'we use the Frame utility function from the Mitsuba rendering framework to construct the rotation transformation R.'
findings.narrowest_supportable_form: 'md-rt keeps Sionna's stock electromagnetic settings but modifies the ray launcher, replacing the spherical Fibonacci lattice with a cone aimed at the target.'

findings.headline: H6 clause 'propeller material Wood' and 'stock EM parameters' - both verbatim.
findings.quote: p3 Table I 'Parameters Setup' (extracted cleanly as text, not an image): 'Waveform OFDM-based | Number of OFDM symbols 2048 | OFDM symbol duration 50us | Rotating propellers 1 | Blades per propeller 2 | Propeller radius 10.55cm | Propeller material Wood'.  p3 prose: 'The model's coordinates are located at its geometric center, and electromagnetic parameters such as conductivity are based on Sionna's built-in settings.'

findings.headline: md-rt claims only kinematic results - and this closes X-C14: it did NOT compute a dynamic RCS.
findings.what_is_true: Counts over the full 6-page text: dBsm 0, 'dB' 0 (the paper never prints a decibel), SNR 0, 'physical optics' 0, SBR 0, UTD 0, 'scattering coefficient' 0, Fresnel 0, 'calibrat*' 0, CFAR 0, 'false alarm' 0, 'detection probability' 0. 'RCS'/'radar cross' 4 hits, ALL in the introduction's motivation plus reference [5] - never a computed value. The validation is period and maximum-shift agreement with the analytic Eq. (7) plus the qualitative envelope shape.
findings.quote: p4: 'According to Eq. (7), the calculated maximum Micro-Doppler frequency shift is 1562 Hz. The rotation period derived from the angular velocity, T = 2pi/omega = 0.04 s, matches perfectly with the simulation results.'  and 'the Micro-Doppler modulation should then appear as two symmetric filled sinusoidal envelopes around zero frequency ... which conform to the theoretical expectation.'
findings.note: X-C14 settled: pw04_data.py's open possibility that md-rt computed a 'dynamic RCS' is closed. It did not.

findings.headline: NEW AND IT MATTERS FOR H8: md-rt never puts a drone in Sionna. It puts ONE propeller.
findings.what_is_true: Table I: 'Rotating propellers 1', 'Blades per propeller 2'. The targets are Sionna's built-in reflector model, then 1 / 2 / 3 / 6 point scatterers, then a single Blender blade model. No airframe, no body, no multi-rotor assembly, despite the title 'Multirotor UAVs'.
findings.quote: p3: 'The target consists of either Sionna's built-in reflector model or a physical model of a propeller modeled using Blender.'  p6 conclusion: 'we demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of Sionna RT in capturing the Micro-Doppler effects caused by a single UAV's rotor motions.'
findings.consequence: In the H8 funnel md-rt must be recorded as 'rotor-only mesh, no airframe' - weaker counter-evidence than a whole-drone mesh would be.

findings.headline: Two more md-rt facts worth carrying, including a factor-of-10 internal inconsistency in the paper.
findings.what_is_true: (a) The paper states its own novelty in exactly the shape of our H8 neighbourhood. (b) Blade size is internally inconsistent by 10x: Table I says the propeller RADIUS is 10.55 cm, while Section IV-B says the blade LENGTH is 1.055 meters. Never quote one without flagging the other.
findings.quote: p1: 'To date, no research has systematically employed ray tracing to model and analyze signal spectrum variations caused by rotational motions of multirotor UAVs.'  p3 Table I: 'Propeller radius 10.55cm'.  p4: 'Under the conditions of a blade length of 1.055 meters, constant rotational speed, and fixed azimuth angle, the range of Micro-Doppler frequency shifts increases linearly with the carrier frequency'.
findings.note: Also quotable, p4: 'considering that the minimum spatial resolution in Sionna is 0.01 m, the number of scattering centers can be regarded as approaching infinity.' - their own statement of the engine's geometric floor.

findings.headline: H9 holds, including the symbol forms the ledger worried about.
findings.claim: OpenISAC contains CFAR / false alarm / detection probability zero times.
findings.what_is_true: Counted here from scratch over the complete 16-page text layer: CFAR 0, 'constant false alarm' 0, 'false alarm' 0 in any form, P_FA symbol forms 0, P_D symbol forms 0, 'detection probability' 0, 'probability of detection' 0, ROC 0, 'missed detection' 0, Neyman 0, GLRT 0. 'threshold' appears 4 times and NONE is a detection threshold: two are the synchronisation correlation ratio rho_th = 100, one is a lock-loss signal-strength threshold, one is a timing-error trigger.
findings.quote: p8: 'with a threshold rho_th. The threshold is selected above the noise-only correlation floor to avoid false synchronization, while remaining sufficiently low to accept the synchronization peak at relatively low SNR. In the reported experiments, rho_th = 100.'
findings.consequence: report01's statement that OpenISAC leaves the Pfa-calibrated detection gap open is safe, and is the strongest surviving support for our detection-side contribution.

findings.headline: OpenISAC is NOT a Sionna paper and must never be counted in the Sionna funnel.
findings.what_is_true: 'Sionna' 4 hits: three inside one related-work sentence on p2, one in reference [19]. No Sionna simulation is run anywhere. It is a USRP testbed paper ('USRP' 22 hits).
findings.quote: p2: 'NVIDIA Sionna and the Sionna Research Kit are also important open-source tools for wireless communication research, including ray-tracing-based channel modeling and SDR-enabled communication prototyping [19]. However, they primarily target commu[nication]...'  p16 ref [19]: 'J. Hoydis, S. Cammerer, F. Ait Aoudia, M. Nimier-David, L. Maggi, G. Marcus, A. Vem, and A. Keller, "Sionna," https://nvlabs.github.io/sionna/, 2022, version 2.0.1.'
findings.note: Side fact worth keeping: OpenISAC pins Sionna version 2.0.1 - the same version we run.

findings.headline: OpenISAC is a preprint per the PDF; the survey's 'IEEE IoT-J 2026' is not supported by any document on disk.
findings.what_is_true: Page-1 margin stamp 'arXiv:2601.03535v2  [eess.SP]  6 Jul 2026'; no journal header, no DOI; 'Internet of Things Journal' / 'IoT-J' 0 hits; PDF producer metadata 'arXiv GenPDF'. The census and src/make_report01_prior.py are right; the survey is wrong.
findings.caveat: Absence of a journal header in an arXiv v2 does not prove non-acceptance. If an IoT-J acceptance exists it is web-only and, by our own rule, must be labelled as such at every citation.

quotable_block_for_reports.engine_claim_en: Sionna RT's stock path solver supports four surface interactions - specular reflection, diffuse reflection, refraction and first-order diffraction. Specular reflection is a Fresnel-coefficient multiplication (Technical Report v2, eq. 127-130, p.44-46); diffuse reflection is an empirical scattering-coefficient model with a normalised scattering pattern (eq. 164-174, p.50-52). The 59-page report contains no occurrence of 'physical optics', 'induced current', 'radar cross section' or 'RCS', and its single 'surface integral' hit is a Wikipedia reference cited for the radio-map area integral.
quotable_block_for_reports.scope_guard_en: Sionna RT does use shooting-and-bouncing of rays - the term appears 48 times - but as a candidate generator feeding an image method, with exactly one ray spawned per interaction. It carries no physical-optics surface integral.
